_doc: Canonical per-platform audience/algorithm content-fit reference. Single source of truth consumed by (1) content_guides.py PLATFORM_GUIDES 'Audience fit:' lines, (2) the marked <!-- PLATFORM-FIT --> blocks in every *-content-ops SKILL.md (.devin + .cursor), (3) the company-brain 'Platform Content Fit' doc via platform-fit-ops/scripts/platform_fit_sync.py. Edit here, then run the sync script — never hand-edit the generated blocks.

linkedin.guide_line: thought leadership and industry insights, educational/how-to content (PDF uploads become swipeable carousels), personal stories with a business lesson, contrarian takes, short hook-driven text or sub-30s vertical video; roughly 4 educational posts per 1 soft promo and 1 hard promo; the 2026 feed uses LLM-embedding retrieval beyond your network plus a generative ranker — original specific posts beat recycled thought-leadership and engagement bait, and meaningful comments in the first hour decide distribution
bullets: Thought leadership & industry insights; educational/how-to content — PDF document uploads render as swipeable carousels and perform strongly.
Personal stories with a business lesson; contrarian takes that spark constructive comments; short hook-driven text or sub-30s vertical video.

2026 feed: LLM-embedding retrieval ('Profile Relevance') surfaces relevant posts beyond your network; a Generative Recommender scores predicted click/read/like/comment/share. It actively downranks engagement bait and recycled thought-leadership — original, specific, expert content wins.
Optimize for dwell time + meaningful comments in the first hour. Rough cadence: ~4 educational posts per 1 soft promo and 1 hard promo.
Cadence (Buffer 2026, 2M+ posts): 2–5 posts/week is the measured sweet spot; LinkedIn posts have a long shelf life so consistency beats bursts.

twitter.guide_line: the real-time conversational feed — serialized text threads for complex topics, live commentary on breaking news, and sharp shareable takes; immediacy and wit beat polish; the 2026 ranker is the open-sourced Grok-based model weighting dwell/read-through, replies and quotes over raw likes
bullets: Real-time conversational feed: serialized text threads for complex topics, live commentary on breaking news/industry events, and sharp shareable takes/memes. Immediacy and wit beat polish.
2026: X open-sourced its Grok-based ranking model (Aug 2026) — it weighs time-spent, read-through, replies and quotes heavily; posts that hold attention past the fold travel further than like-bait.
Cadence (Buffer 2026): 3–4 posts/day — the timeline moves fast and more volume compounds reach when quality holds.

instagram.guide_line: aesthetics and lifestyle curation — Reels get the strongest algorithmic distribution (trending audio, fast hook), carousels suit step-by-step guides and before/after transformations, Stories are the casual daily-engagement lane; watch time, sends and shares now outrank likes — make content people forward to a friend
bullets: Aesthetics/lifestyle curation: **Reels** get the strongest distribution (vertical video, trending audio, hook in the first second); **carousels** (≤10 slides) suit step-by-step guides and before/after transformations; **Stories** are the casual daily-engagement lane.
2026 signals: watch time, **sends** and shares are the top ranking inputs (per Instagram's head) — content engineered to be sent to a friend outperforms content engineered to be liked.
Prioritize visual quality — the caption supports the media.
Cadence (Buffer 2026): 3–5 feed posts/week is the sweet spot (+12% reach vs 1–2/wk); Reels can run higher if quality holds.

facebook.guide_line: an older, community-oriented demographic — external link shares and news articles outperform here vs LinkedIn/IG, group-style discussion and recommendations resonate, and long-form video or live streams get strong reach; predicted engagement and time-spent drive ranking
bullets: Older, community-oriented demographic: external link shares + news articles outperform here vs LinkedIn/IG; group-style discussion, recommendations, and long-form video or live streams get strong reach.
2026 signals: predicted engagement and time spent on content outrank clicks — earn attention, not just link taps.
Both surfaces below already fit this — personal build-log = community content; page link/news posts = the link-share lane.
Cadence (Buffer 2026): 1–2 posts/day on the Page; predicted engagement and time-spent outrank raw link taps.

threads.guide_line: conversational micro-blogging — short authentic takes, opinion hooks, and reply-style conversation outperform polished brand copy; predicted engagement and view time drive the feed, and questions that invite replies travel furthest
bullets: Conversational micro-updates and authentic takes — short opinion hooks and human-sounding posts beat polished brand copy; reply-style conversation drives distribution.
2026 signals: predicted engagement + view time; posts ending in a genuine question tend to earn the replies that feed distribution.
Cadence (Buffer 2026): 3–4 posts/week building toward daily — the feed rewards consistent conversational presence.

tiktok.guide_line: the For You Page prioritizes watch-time and engagement over production quality and largely ignores follower count — raw, authentic, or humorous vertical video beats slick ads; trending audio, challenges, and educational micro-content all travel; hook in the first three seconds
bullets: Watch-time + engagement over production quality: raw, authentic, or humorous vertical video beats slick ads; trending audio/challenges and educational micro-content (life hacks, niche explainers like #TechTok) all travel. Hook in the first second — the caption supports the video.
2026 signals: the FYP is interest-graph driven — follower count is not a direct ranking factor, so a small account's great post can out-reach a big account's weak one.
Cadence (Buffer 2026): 2–5 videos/week — the biggest view lift comes from going 1 → 2–5/wk; keyword in caption + on-screen text + spoken in the first seconds covers FYP and TikTok Search.

bluesky.guide_line: chronological Following feed makes posting time matter more than on algorithmic platforms — the Discover feed plus 50,000+ community-built custom feeds surface posts by topic keywords and hashtags, so niche-specific tags and self-contained posts earn feed inclusion; threads format for depth, and early replies/reposts decide traction
bullets: No single hidden algorithm: the Following feed is reverse-chronological, Discover is Bluesky's own recommender, and 50k+ custom feeds rank by their own topic rules — earning a spot in the feeds your audience pins matters more than follower count.
Write posts that stand alone (feed browsers lack context), use specific topic keywords/hashtags for feed matching, and post consistently — feed refresh cycles surface recent posts, not archives.
Cadence (Buffer 2026, 3M+ posts): consistent posting through the day beats bursts; weekends are the peak (Saturday ~5pm top slot, 4–7pm best window, weekday evenings 6–9pm next best).
